  "reference_object": "vinyl siding coursing (~8 in exposed per lath) and standard 32 in exterior door width, used to gauge distances",

  "requires_member_action": true,
  "decision": "manual_review",
  "needs_more_photos": true,
  "missing_views": [
    "Wider shot showing the full wall length between the electric meter (photo 11) and the red-shutter corner (photos 12-15) to confirm continuous, unobstructed wall footage",
    "A shot showing the distance from the red-shutter wall to the paver walkway/deck to confirm 5 ft clearance is met",
    "A ground-level shot of the red-shutter window to confirm sill height and whether it is an operable ground-level window",
    "A photo showing the gas meter and AC unit together on the same wall to measure the exact gap between them and the 3 ft/6 ft gas exclusion zone"
  ],
  "justification": "The site shows a gas meter (photos 1-4) that excludes roughly 6 ft of contiguous wall, and an AC unit (photos 6-9) occupying further wall space with a wall-mounted box above it that needs to stay clear-both reduce usable width along that stretch. The electric meter (photo 11) sits close to a corner that leads directly into a deck/stair area, leaving little clear run before the obstruction. Rounding the corner, photos 12-15 show a promising stretch of plain siding wall with mulch/dirt ground and only decorative, movable foundation rocks, which could offer 3ft+ width and adequate footprint. However, a paver walkway runs parallel to this wall (photo 12) and a shuttered window sits near the corner, so it isn't clear whether the 5 ft facing clearance and window/walkway setback rules are satisfied, or whether this is a secondary walkway that must stay clear. The harness route from the electric meter to this candidate wall appears short (roughly 10-15 ft based on siding panel counts) but the exact length and unobstructed continuity across the corner are not fully confirmed. Because the strongest candidate spot has unresolved clearance/window/walkway questions and the exact route length is borderline, this requires manual review rather than an outright pass or reject."
}
